facts.claim: Flight SK916, an Airbus A330-300 registered LN-RKR, departed New York JFK at 7:24 PM on October 23, 29 minutes late, and landed at Newark at 10:58 PM after three hours and 34 minutes in the air after a technical issue.

Passengers waited around an hour at baggage claim before being told luggage could not be removed from the aircraft, and the QR code system would not accept missing-bag reports because they had not reached their destination.
Past midnight, SAS emailed passengers asking them to arrange their own accommodation, offering reimbursement of up to $280 (€250) per room.
SAS confirmed to TV 2 that the flight returned due to a possible technical fault and was being inspected in Newark; the aircraft flew to Copenhagen the following day as flight SK910.

Under EU261, airlines must provide free hotel accommodation for overnight delays plus airport-hotel transport, and passengers may be entitled to $672 (€600) compensation for delays of four hours or more on flights over 3,500 kilometers.

zh.title: SAS班機SK916大西洋上空因技術問題折返：旅客深夜滯留紐瓦克自覓旅館
zh.summary: SAS班機SK916自紐約甘迺迪機場飛往哥本哈根途中因技術問題折返，轉降紐瓦克。旅客在行李無法取回、訂位紀錄消失的情況下過夜，航空公司請旅客自行安排住宿，並提供每房最高280美元補助。
body: SAS班機SK916原定10月23日晚間自紐約甘迺迪機場飛往哥本哈根，機型為空中巴士A330-300、機身編號LN-RKR。班機晚間7時24分起飛，較表定晚29分鐘；飛行約2小時後，旅客從機上地圖發現航向不對，機組隨後表示飛機出現技術問題，機長認為不宜繼續橫越大西洋。班機飛行3小時34分後於晚間10時58分轉降紐瓦克自由國際機場，跑道上已有消防車與救護車待命。

落地後的混亂持續到深夜。旅客在行李轉盤等候約1小時後，才被告知行李無法自機上卸下；航空公司提供的行李遺失申報QR碼，也因旅客未抵達原目的地而無法受理。數小時過去仍無新的航班資訊，訂位紀錄甚至自SAS應用程式中消失；過了午夜後，SAS才以電子郵件請旅客自行安排住宿，並提供每房最高280美元補助。旅客Michael Flarup表示，他搶到當地最後幾間房之一，但離開時仍有許多旅客滯留機場（EWR），且多次致電客服也無法得知家人兩件行李的下落。

SAS向丹麥媒體TV2證實，班機因可能出現技術故障而返航，飛機正在紐瓦克接受檢查，但未說明故障性質，也未解釋為何轉降紐瓦克而非甘迺迪機場。追蹤資料顯示，涉事飛機隔日以SK910班機飛往哥本哈根。由於SK916由歐洲籍航空公司營運且目的地為哥本哈根，適用歐盟EU261航空旅客權益規則：航空公司須為過夜延誤提供免費住宿與機場往返交通，另須提供餐飲；延誤4小時以上、航程逾3500公里的旅客，也可能獲得600歐元補償。

en.title: SAS flight SK916 turns back over the Atlantic, leaving passengers stranded overnight in Newark
en.summary: SAS flight SK916 from New York JFK to Copenhagen diverted to Newark after a technical issue more than three hours into the flight, leaving passengers without their bags or new flight details well past midnight.
body: Flight SK916, operated by an Airbus A330-300 registered LN-RKR, was scheduled to leave New York JFK at 6:55 PM local time on Friday, October 23, for an overnight flight to Copenhagen, due to arrive at 8:40 AM on Saturday. Tracking data shows the aircraft departed at 7:24 PM, 29 minutes behind schedule. Around two hours into the flight, passenger Michael Flarup, who was traveling home to Copenhagen with his son, noticed on the in-flight map that the aircraft was heading in the wrong direction. Cabin crew then told passengers the aircraft had developed a technical issue and the pilots did not feel comfortable continuing across the Atlantic. The aircraft landed at Newark at 10:58 PM after three hours and 34 minutes in the air, with fire trucks and ambulances waiting on the runway.

The difficulties continued after landing. Passengers waited around an hour at baggage claim before being told their luggage could not be removed from the aircraft, and a QR code issued to report missing bags would not accept their reports because they had not reached their original destination. Several hours passed without an update, and Flarup said his booking disappeared from the SAS app altogether. By then it was past midnight, before SAS emailed passengers asking them to arrange their own accommodation and offering reimbursement of up to $280 (€250) per room. Flarup said he managed to book one of the last available hotel rooms in the area, but many passengers were still stranded at Newark when he and his son left, and repeated calls to SAS support could not establish where the family's two suitcases were.

Flarup said: "Safety comes first. But the handling of hundreds of stranded passengers afterwards really needs to be better. People need clear information and a way to get home, especially in the middle of the night." SAS confirmed to Danish outlet TV 2 that the flight returned due to a possible technical fault and that the aircraft was being inspected in Newark, but did not elaborate on the nature of the fault or why the aircraft was sent to Newark instead of JFK. Tracking data shows the aircraft flew to Copenhagen the following day as flight SK910. Because SK916 was operated by a European airline and bound for Copenhagen, it falls under EU261: airlines must provide free hotel accommodation for overnight delays plus transport between the airport (EWR) and hotel, and meals and refreshments; passengers may also be entitled to $672 (€600) in compensation for delays of four hours or more on flights over 3,500 kilometers.
